messages.text: Take {gift_item}. A good village keeps its friends fed and standing.
Here, {gift_item}. It is honest work to send someone off with provisions.
Good. {tested_villager} has a sound nose for {gift_item}. Fresh advice, clean cut.
If {tested_villager} liked {gift_item}, then the cut was right.
Bad cut, then. For {gift_subject}, I would set down {gift_item} and bring {alternative_gift}.
Some gifts spoil in the telling. Try {alternative_gift}; that should suit {gift_subject} better.

openings.text: Mind the smokehouse. What do you need?

closings.text: Back to keeping meat salted and safe, then.

lines.text: A smokehouse tells you fast who understands patience.
Empty hooks before supper can frighten a village more than thunder.
Food decides whether a scare becomes a disaster.
If you smell smoke, that is supper being planned properly.
Salt is patient. That is why it keeps food better than most people keep promises.
Empty hooks tell a village to start worrying before anyone says it aloud.
A full cellar has ended more arguments here than any speech ever did.
My jokes are like my cuts: better when nobody rushes me.
That was stale enough to leave on the shelf.
People think about courage until supper is late. Then they think about supper.
A village with good stores can make careful choices instead of desperate ones.
Once the smokehouse door stuck shut, and everyone became helpful very quickly.
I have carved gristle with more grace than you brought here.

pacify.text: Fine. I have work to get back to, and anger spoils the day.
Too lean an offer. Bring {emerald_cost} {emeralds} if you want this cut clean.
No. I know bad meat, and I know bad apologies.
